newsitem.title: EGYPT: Jordan to follow Arab decision on summit - minister.
newsitem.headline: Jordan to follow Arab decision on summit - minister.

text.p: Jordan's prime minister said on Sunday that his country would participate in this year's Middle East economic conference between Israel and its Arab neighbours only if other Arab countries decided to attend.

"If the Arabs decide not to participate and they see that the greater Arab interest is that they do not go, then that would apply to everyone," Abdul-Salam al-Majali told reporters after meeting Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
"And if they decided to go then we are with them in going."

Israeli-Palestinian talks collapsed in March after Israel enraged Palestinians by starting work on a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. Palestinians and Israeli troops have had running clashes in the West Bank town of Hebron for a week.
The annual conferences, launched in Casablanca in 1994, are meant to promote peace in the Middle East through trade and economic cooperation between Israel and its Arab neighbours.
Jordan's Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah was quoted on Saturday in Ad-Dustour newspaper as saying that his country would attend this year's summit, due to be held in Doha, Qatar.

Tarawnah said he saw the meeting as a "golden opportunity" for business in the region and said Arab states could use it to overcome differences with Israel. "We have a clear position...to attend the conference if it is held," he said.
Saudi Arabia has already said it would not attend the conference in November. Other key Arab states, including Egypt and Morocco, have decided to wait for progress in the peace talks.
